summary: The exact candidate fixes duplicate grammar compilation and masking for ordinary TP and correctly broadcasts entry-rank token IDs, but explicitly retains compile-and-mask-on-every-rank behavior for speculative TP and active context parallelism. It is therefore a valid partial fix, not a full resolution of the original unqualified feature request.

tests.what_was_measured: On recorded base 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365, a simulated non-entry TP rank made one backend lookup and received a Future, reproducing duplicate grammar compilation submission.
At exact candidate efa4ba5a75b21b2867e55582e7b1b98f7cf2b81f, ordinary TP made zero backend lookups on a simulated non-entry rank and carried PlaceholderGrammarObject.
Both remaining counterexamples reproduced: speculative TP and active context-parallel TP each made one backend grammar lookup on the simulated non-entry rank and received a Future.
The candidate's focused compatibility and regression suite passed 97 tests.
An independent real two-process Gloo call through the candidate sampler broadcast rank 0's token, producing [(0, 3), (1, 3)] from initially divergent values.
All candidate-changed Python source paths compiled successfully under the prepared interpreter.
The candidate diff has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: The environment probe found one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), but this review did not claim a single-GPU smoke as evidence for the distributed TP contract. True TP, speculative TP, and context-parallel TP require unavailable multi-GPU architecture.

remaining_counterexamples: With tensor parallelism and speculative decoding active, tp_grammar_entry_only is false, so a non-entry TP rank still submits a grammar backend lookup and retains per-rank grammar masking.
With tensor parallelism and an active attention context-parallel group, tp_grammar_entry_only is false, so applicable non-entry ranks still compile grammars and apply masks.
remaining_limitations: Only one GPU was assigned; true multi-GPU ordinary TP serving, speculative TP, context-parallel TP, and end-to-end overhead measurements were unavailable.
The independent two-process Gloo collective test validates token broadcast mechanics only and does not qualify distributed ROCm serving.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture cannot supply speculative-TP or context-parallel distributed architecture and was not used as substitute evidence.
No native source files changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
